speaker: Unknown
quote_text: Is that your toughest day as a skipper? >> Uh yeah, about there I think, yeah. Um yeah, full credit to Bangladesh. They they batted superbly this morning when it probably did a little bit and then um yeah, carried it on into the afternoon and uh played the spin well. Um yeah, aggressive at times and absorbed pressure at times. So, yeah, full credit to them. They batted beautifully today. >> Is your side >> Yeah, absolutely. I mean with the quality we've got in our dressing room, I'm I'm sure everybody's still looking at a a way to win this game of cricket. Um obviously we've got to get these last four wickets as as cheaply as possible and then um yeah, putting probably two really good days of batting which is going to be hard work, no doubt, but um yeah, like I said, the boys in the dressing room um you know, full faith that we've got the caliber we can do it. >> Uh obviously yeah, the bowlers and yourself toiled there, but there are periods where things just weren't happening. What do you sort of put that down to? >> Yeah, uh test cricket I suppose. That's the way it is. It's obviously a hot day out there and um the wicket looks like it's flattened out a little bit like a a little bit more than it was the morning of day one. So, um yeah, like I said, they batted really well. We tried um a few different plans, wide, straight, um spin, some some bumpers from Marnus at the end there to try and try and grab a wicket and and see if we can go through, but um yeah, they batted nicely and and we're going to have to come up with some more plans for tomorrow. >> How different did that feel to some of the test matches last summer given I guess Bangladesh, you know, a five for 250 odd today, they really made you work for it. They weren't going to sort of beat themselves I suppose. >> Yeah, it's just um like I said before, test cricket, good old grind, back into it, hot hot weather, flat wicket and um yeah, it's it's not always going to be two days where the ball's flying around and and boundaries and wickets. So, um good old-fashioned grind again and and we're going to be up for the fight again for the last three days. >> Hey, can you just cast your mind back to to yesterday and the the batting um like the conditions obviously, you know, decided to decided to to to bat first. How I suppose did you you see the conditions in in your time out there? >> Yeah, I mean I think we all agree that it it nipped around um enough on in the first 2 hours there and then probably got a little bit flatter probably when I got out there it didn't feel like it was doing a hell of a lot um and Smudge said it died down quite a bit since the first session so um yeah, I suppose we just lost a a couple of too many wickets in that in that first 2 hours there to to really put any pressure back on the ball through the middle there so um yeah, full credit they bowled really well again um in that in that morning session hit the right areas and and you know, made us play and there was a little bit of assistance off the wicket. >> Pat's pace noticeably dropped off in that last session. Do you just put that down to the heat and the conditions and >> Uh you'd have to ask him mate to be honest with you. >> [laughter] >> I think everybody might have dropped a little bit after a full day in 32° and and the first hit out back after a long stint off so um yeah, it's a question for him I think. >> If you put a chase of 170 it hasn't been done very often in test cricket. So what what what sort of approach do you think you're going to have to and you're going to make a for a natural game What's what's in your sort of approach going to have to take? >> Uh I think you know, we've got some naturally aggressive batters already to to move the scoreboard along. Um you know, hopefully the the wicket stays quite true and nice and we can put some pressure back on their bowlers. Um but yeah, like I said there's still 3 days left of cricket here and you know, a day and a half of really good batting at a at a half-decent clip gets us right back in this in this contest, you know, batting last in a in a test match and a and a hopefully worn wicket could be could be tricky if it is a little small chase so I think that's our obvious obvious way to to win the game. >> How much energy do you put into bowling wickets for a longer period of time or having to bowl a lot of overs in the last couple of sessions and also in a hot day just all the day? >> Yeah, it's tough. It was hot out there. I think um you know, me and Kez spoke at the end of the day there saying that was that that felt like a a long day. It was you know, they they tempered their innings really well when they they come out and played some shots early against Gary and then you know, absorbed some nice spells especially when we got the the second new ball. Um we got a couple of wickets and then they managed to hold the momentum again. So yeah, it was a it was a a tough grind no doubt. Um you know, that's test cricket. That's that's cricket at the top level. So um full credit to the way they batted and you know, we're going to come back in the morning hard and try and pick up four wickets and and you know, get up set up off on this on our way to try and win this game. >> Two more folks and then we'll let you >> Um besides regular bowler, you used total eight bowlers today. So what was the reason? What was the tactics behind these? >> Uh yeah, hot day. You know, um you know, we've got the three front line quicks and and Nathan and and like I said, they played him quite well. Nathan the sort of forces to bring some medium pace back on and you know, me and Greeny shared I think maybe 20 overs between us roughly and and chipped in with Marnus Labuschagne as well. So just a a long day test cricket where um it was hot and you know, mindful we've got another innings we're going to have to bowl to to win this game of cricket. So probably didn't want to burn all all three of the big boys, you know, by bowling them 25 in a day on a on a 32 degree day. >> Have you enjoyed the more pace in Darwin also? >> Yeah, it's been fantastic. Yeah, obviously the the crowd's been good and lively. It's it's been a good cricket wicket so far and um yeah, hopefully we've got three more days of exciting cricket here and and put on a good show. >> Do you think it could go to day five this test? >> Yeah, absolutely. Yeah, I see no reason why it can't. Obviously we've got to we've got to put our hand up with the bat. Our our batting group was obviously a little bit disappointing on day one. So we're going to have to put our hand up and and bat long and and bat long periods like they did and put some pressure back on to keep the the scoreboard ticking over. But yeah, it's you know, five day test cricket. The way we're going to win it it's not going to be anywhere near, you know, other than late day day five. So uh I'm sure we're up for the contest. >> Thanks everyone. Thank you. Thanks mate. Cheers.
title: 'A good ol' grind!'  Webster on a tough Day 2 against Bangladesh | Australia Press Conference
